notes.title: Major Content Preview: Shorter Raids, Shopkeepers, and New Unit Management!
notes.content:
Hello everyone! 

Back in June, we announced that we would be making some major changes to Sons of Valhalla to solve some of the feedback we’ve been getting, especially in terms of “big picture” items like game structure.

We wanted to give a small glimpse of the things are changing and how we envision the game evolving going forward.

[h2]Campaign Structure[/h2]

A major point of criticism has always been how levels feel a bit too long and lack variety. To combat this, we’ve made a radical decision to break the levels up and make them smaller, as well as introduce a new overview map that will display all of the control points available. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38733779/933d77042267aca9ec8fdf25d1fe1c3c4151a25c.jpg[/img]
Raiding a point should take no longer than 20 minutes now, after which you return to the overview map and pick your next target. You need to make sure you have sufficient troops, though – the battles will now be more intense, and sometimes you can lose all your units and be forced to retreat.

If you start the raid on one of the points and are successful in the battle, you can loot hacksilver and gold to buy more units and upgrades. If your units are defeated, you can try to reach the rescue ship and carry out another attack with fresh units. 

There is also a time element to this - a storm is coming, and it will steadily push you south. When it arrives at your location, any points on the same vertical axis will be locked off, forcing you to go south instead. This type of level management is not new, but it has proven itself. This also gives us the opportunity to design levels much more freely, without having to pay attention to the old, narrow level management.

[h2]The Story[/h2]
A quick note on the story - despite the new campaign structure, the story will remain largely as-is, although we may remove one or two cutscenes. There are boss levels on the map that have been placed in a strategic way so the player has to master this level if he wants to continue. The player then fights the boss and - if you win - you will be able to continue your journey.

[h2]Death & Rebirth[/h2]
Death will continue to be your constant companion in Sons of Valhalla – not every raid will be successful, and this time, death is permanent. The old rune system is being abolished, but the rune stones themselves will remain. Odin will still give you the opportunity to exchange rune stones you find for advantages for the next trip. So you can fail, but you make more progress with each attempt to save Raya. 

The system will now compensate the player for dying and will not punish the player anymore, like in the old system.

[h2]Unit Management[/h2]
Before you start a raid, you have to decide which units you want to take with you. To do this, you have to buy units before each raid. It is an advantage to take a closer look at the next target. An indication of the fortification's strength can be seen at every point on the world map. If you have a triple shield, you should definitely pack siege weapons if you have them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38733779/57a5a844f0a5164383bd61388d2ed9833ba89d9d.jpg[/img]
You can give units and yourself a special ability. However, these abilities have a different effect than the old rune system. If you assign an ability to the unit, all other units of this type have the same ability. This means that abilities will have more impact on the game than the old rune system did.

[h2]Going to the Shoppe[/h2]
But how do you get skills now that there are no more runes? Fear not, because Capitalism(™) has come to Viking-age England! Skills, provisions, arrows, and mercenary units can all be purchased via the new “shops.” There are 4 different types of shops, and the shops are randomly distributed on the map after the game starts:

[b]General[/b]
This shop sells provisions and consumables such as projectiles (arrows)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38733779/d4b900e4ef94f6627168c300e2288cd41b6b25d6.gif[/img]
[b]Armory[/b]
Items that have skills are sold here. One of the most important shops by far.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38733779/1d1f4cb306728170afa4fb0d65f8c5279f3e05c0.gif[/img]
[b]Mercenary agent[/b]
This gentleman specializes in arranging mercenaries. A contract signed here allows you to hire this unit in the future.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38733779/4f94ab51f57142ae90a417169e0bfe9a8f9a3d23.gif[/img]
[b]Shipyard[/b]
A larger ship to accommodate more crew? No problem; your ship is in good hands here.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38733779/cd44ec72c6b657020231888758fb1e4291a2a200.gif[/img]
I hope you enjoyed this glimpse as to what the upcoming update will look like.

- Pixel Chest Games

notes.title: A First Look at Upcoming Changes to Sons of Valhalla
notes.content:
Hello everyone!
As some of you may have noticed, things have become a bit quiet about Sons of Valhalla. That doesn't mean that we aren't working on the game - the opposite is the case.
As you can imagine we are not satisfied with the current state of the reviews. There are several points that were mentionend quite often in the reviews, which made us think about some design decisions and we're now at the point to take a radical step to solve them.
After a long back and forth, we realized that unfortunately there are no "simple" solutions.

What does this mean for Sons of Valhalla?

We have already started to remove and renew some systems. We focus on replay value, creating a more fun battle experience and a new progression system.

This whole restructuring will take time. Time we actually don't have, because we had planned to already work on additional content by now. But if a game isn't good enough, you have to change something or you'll go down, which would be a shame for you, the players, because many of you expected a better game, and for us as developers, because our future as game developers depends on it.

We kindly ask you to give us the time to give the game a way better foundation for further content - and most important: a future! We appreciate the support we got and the valuable feedback we received! 

Thank you!

notes.title: Sons Of Valhalla Review: A mostly brilliant tac-and-slash tug of war
notes.content:
Like an aggressively competitive thane at a reindeer-piss guzzling contest, 2D tac-and-slash roguelite Sons Of Valhalla never lets up the pace for even a moment. Whether you’re charging across its pixel-art battlefields slashing and burning increasingly tough-to-crack strongholds, or making quick decisions to get the upper hand in its tug-of-war tactics, the only times Thorald is not doing cool violence, commanding others to do cool violence, or upgrading his camps so that he may act in cooler and more violent ways, is when he’s restoring stamina with a cool slug of mead or violently gnawing at health-boosting meat.

Viking Thorald Olavson is a man possessed. A rival Jarl burnt his village and nicked his wife Raya. In his quest to find her, he’s prepared to do anything - even visit England. As Thorald, you’ll butcher your way up a chain of command in your search for Raya across six stages, each of which sits somewhere between the side-scrolling tactics of Kingdom Two Crowns, the lane strategy of a Warpips, and the slashy/blocky/shooty/dodgy of any 2D ARPG you care to name.

notes.title: Update #6
notes.content:
Hello folks, we have another update for you!

Some time has passed since the last update and we have been busy  implementing a lot of the things you mentioned and requested. 
First and foremost: The game now feels much faster! Updates in the  respective buildings have been compressed, the command system now allows  to communicate more directly with the units, and much more. 
Here's an overview of the most important changes made during the last  few weeks: 
 
[b]Save & Load [/b]
One of the most complex changes is probably the Save&Load system. Yes,  it's finally possible to save! The game will autosave every time the  player replenishes supplies or when the level is finished. 
There are a total of 4 save slots available. 
 
[b]Commands [/b]
Based on your feedback, we have redesigned the Command menu. It is now  possible to communicate more directly with the units and, for example,  only let archers or melee fighters attack. 
But if you don't need this kind of precision, you can still command your units together. 
 
[b]Champions[/b] 
Champions are special units that can aid you in the way you play. Like  all of your units, they respond to orders. 
There are currently four champions: the Shaman (heals your units), the  Berserker (strong against infantry), the Shieldmaiden (strong and  enduring against infantry), and the Blacksmith (strong against gates and  barricades). 
For example, if you're playing resource-friendly, the shaman would be a  good choice. It would heal your units and would prevent you from taking big casualties. 
It's up to you which strategy and which champion you want to choose. Be  aware that champions can only be hired at a captured outpost. It is not  possible to hire more than one champion per outpost. 
 
[b]Mini bosses [/b]
After some successful testing, we have added the first two mini-bosses to the first level. 
They defend their outposts with more devotion than their minions 😉 
We will gradually adjust the strength over time. 
 
[b]Outpost [/b]
A conquered outpost now has a harbor right from the start to cut long  and unnecessary walks. If you've earned some money it's also possible to  build a stockpile. 
 
[b]Mead hall[/b] 
Now you have the opportunity upgrade Thoralds health and stamina. 
These upgrades are for all levels. 
 
[b]AI changes[/b] 
A huge issue that slowed down the game was the intelligence of the  units. These will now run automatically to the recent conquered point.  In addition, archers can be released more easily from the towers with  the help of the "follow" command. Archers will automatically seek an  elevated position (tower) if one is available nearby. 
 
[b]Demo[/b] 
We also made a lot of other small adjustments and are now ready to  replace the current demo. 
We will transfer the current status to the demo by the end of June at  the latest. 
 
[b]Beta tester[/b] 
There are also some good news for all Kickstarter followers "Tier  Backer": At the beginning of the next month we will integrate the next level and  we'll also invite all beta testers! 
 
That's all for now. Thank you for your attention! 
 
Best 
[b]Sons of Valhalla Team[/b]

notes.title: Update #2
notes.content:
Hello folks, we have another update for you! As announced in the last update, we are currently overhauling several systems:

[h1]Runes/Perk[/h1]
The new rune system will replace the old techtree and it's almost ready. We needed a lot more time for this system than planned, but we believe that it was worth it. Runes can still be found in the world or looted from enemies. But not every rune is the same:

[b]Rarity[/b]
There are 4 rarities: Common, Rare , Epic and Legendary. All rarities are identified by different colors. The runes attribute is enhanced by the rarity. For example, a common rune has a damage value of +10 and a legendary +30. This system is not new, but it offers a lot of variety and a high replay value.

[b]Categories/Slots[/b]
As you already know from the old Techtree system, there will be 4 categories. Each category has a limited number of free slots that can be expanded as the game progresses. For example you still have the option to focus on the fight first and then take care of your economy later.


[h1]Dialogue system[/h1]
The new dialogue system wasn't much of a challenge. However, it took a while to create portraits of each character. Maybe you already recognize some of them 😉 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38733779/0e08ddf64e76d0c9bf759a37ff4b5810b54546cb.png[/img]

We created the new system for a greater visibility of text at distance. For all couch potatoes, and later on for the console versions.


[b]Closing remarks[/b]
Due to the conversion of the old system, we are a little behind our roadmap-timesheet. But we are still making good progress! We were able to win new pixel artists who do an incredibly good job! The team is motivated, what else could you ask for?

If you have any questions, you are very welcome to join our discord!

Best
Sons of Valhalla Team

notes.title: DevBlog #1
notes.content:
Hi guys,

welcome to my first Sons of Valhalla Dev-blog! This month I mainly worked on my online presence. So the Steam page is finally live and you can now also find me on IndieDB and GameJolt. 
Besides that I worked on a lot of little things regarding the game and one of them is how I bring life into trees. I'm going to show you how it works in todays dev blog. 

[b]First of all, I needed a tree like this one:[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38733779/68e37ff0d623c8f03af54d4e7066152be8e601c4.jpg[/img]


This tree is beautiful but if it had some movement it would be even more beautiful to look at. So I took a wind shader from Unity (you can find it in the Lost Crypt demo) to make the tree vibrate.
Because the shader is on the entire tree, the trunk and treetop move at the same time.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38733779/5541470d4c21c2d317b1675289af625a121676c7.gif[/img]

Then I decided to divide the tree into individual parts, so I can equip each part with a different wind speed. This will make the tree look more realistic because the entire treetop will not move evenly.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38733779/a705176164c9e5762c6fbc23d69dc3ef4a969274.jpg[/img]

After the split I put the parts back together and gave each part a different wind speed.
I think the result is really impressive.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38733779/597ed9da6e914dc3c0f9cc73bbecd7e128e2c84f.gif[/img]

To make the tree fit into the background, I created a rim color mask for all parts. With the wind shader it is possible to transfer the light color of the scene onto the tree rim and it looks as if light is shining through the rim. Very cool!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38733779/68ae8b48c2aaeb3cdb53f1ca5e37220e62791f7b.jpg[/img]

Because the tree sometimes loses a few leaves, we definitely had to have a particle effect here. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38733779/67913c1b12b030347ac864a16afe679858456d15.jpg[/img]

The end result is highly impressive, right?
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38733779/622e85d507369cc4a44f76002db693d0e9f795e6.gif[/img]

That's how I make trees dancing in Sons of Valhalla! If you haven't already, please add SOV to your wishlist. I'd really appreciate your support! 

See you in the next dev blog episode!
